steps.body: A line plot puts a number line under the data: each measurement becomes one x above its value, and repeats stack up.
steps.narration: A line plot puts a number line under the data: each measurement becomes one x above its value, and repeats stack up.

widget.prompt: The record 6, 6, 7, 6, 8, 7 became this plot. Verify the transcription: count the x's above 6.
widget.successFeedback: Three — exactly as many x's as the record holds 6s. The transcription is faithful.
widget.partialFeedback: Check the plot against the record: the 6-stack must hold one x per recorded 6, no more, no less.

predict.prompt: The record holds six measurements. How many x's will the finished plot show?
predict.reveal: Every measurement earns its own x; values shared by several get taller stacks, not fewer marks.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g2g build lineplot.
invariants: A display and its data are the same information in two forms: every measurement appears exactly once, and counts survive the trip into stacks, rows, and bars for g2g build lineplot.
misconceptions: Reading a label as a count, dropping repeats while recording, or comparing categories by adding instead of finding the gap.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change to the data would the display be FORCED to show — and what change could it silently hide?

widget.prompt: A line plot shows 6 x's above the number 11. How many data points are at 11?

commonErrors.feedback: That read the LABEL under the stack — the count is how many x's stand on it.
Label and count got added together; only the x's in the stack are data points.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Read the display itself: count what is drawn, and let the stacks, rows, and bars do the remembering.

widget.prompt: You measured five ribbons: 6, 8, 6, 7, 6 cm. Which record keeps ALL the information?

options.label: 6, 8, 6, 7, 6 — every measurement, repeats included
options.feedback: Correct — a record's job is completeness; the three 6s are three real ribbons, not one.

options.label: 6, 7, 8 — just the different values
options.feedback: Dropping repeats erases HOW MANY ribbons hit each length — the very thing a line plot will need.

options.label: The biggest: 8
options.feedback: One number describes one ribbon; four others vanish from that record.

options.label: About 7 each
options.feedback: An average-flavored summary trades away the individual measurements a plot is built from.
